title: (A)I've made a Indie Game and release it after 1month and 1day
author: ePi3354
selftext:
Hi Redditors!

This is my first post, and I wanted to share what I’ve been working on over the past month. I work full time as a software developer (though not in games), so this has been a side project.

At the beginning of October, some friends and I played a few tidy-up games and really enjoyed them. We wished there were more levels, and that more of them supported multiplayer. So I asked Claude to help me prototype a tidy-up game in Godot. Over time, that prototype grew into a cozy fantasy cleanup game with 19 levels and co-op for up to 8 players.

I’ve used a lot of free assets, and one of my biggest concerns has been making the game feel cohesive and personal rather than like a generic AI-generated project. The early version definitely had that “AI slop” feel, but after a lot of iteration, I think it’s starting to feel more natural.

I’m honestly surprised by how much I’ve managed to build in about four weeks: a working demo, 19 levels, and 120 wishlists so far, mostly from sharing the project on Instagram without paid ads.

Do you think I’m seeing it through rose-colored glasses, or does the game feel like it has its own identity? I’d really appreciate feedback on the Steam page or the demo! Thank you

[https://store.steampowered.com/app/5391250/Tidy\_Up\_Ltd\_A\_Cozy\_Coop\_Cleanup/](https://store.steampowered.com/app/5391250/Tidy_Up_Ltd_A_Cozy_Coop_Cleanup/)
